title: Local Response Stability for Certified Two-Step Rollout in Engineering Optimization
abstract_tex: Two-step rollout can require a complete response-dependent continuation partition for every first action. We propose a finite-menu solver that certifies a reference continuation on a response domain and bounds omitted adaptation by its complement probability. A positive-response planning model makes terminal improvement bounded. Posterior residual enclosures, conditional-reward curvature and directed integration produce a checked first-action selection rule, with selective complete projection and unresolved outcomes. A prospectively frozen implementation verifies both local and direct routes on all 43 archived beam-design states at tolerance m0/1000000, with identical selections. Local stability reduces complete projections from 114 to 25, but its checked numerical stage takes 5.47 seconds versus 4.93 seconds for the direct route. Paid engineering replay has mixed outcomes. Source, fixed inputs and per-state records are preserved. The contribution is a response-stability mechanism for certified finite-menu rollout optimization; the evidence establishes model-based numerical applicability, without engineering-policy superiority or deployment savings.
